comparison: Both evaluate IL-15Rα upregulation and bystander activation (C5, C6, C68, C69). OpenEval finds the experimental co-culture data supportive with reasonable mechanistic interpretation. Peer reviewers accept the data but question the mechanistic interpretation, specifically asking whether bystander activation could be driven in tissue rather than blood, marking this as UNCERTAIN versus OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

Both address long COVID associations with immune activation (C7-C9, C31-C34, C83-C88). OpenEval finds the statistical analysis appropriate and conclusions justified despite limited power, marking as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, requesting reanalysis with more granular PASC outcome measures, suggesting the broad symptom count may obscure meaningful associations.

Both evaluate longitudinal resolution of immune activation (C27, C56, C57, C65, C66, C101). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED based on clear temporal resolution across multiple parameters. Peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED, accepting this as 'convincing evidence,' though suggest better presentation of timepoint comparisons.

Both assess SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell responses (C28-C30, C70-C81). OpenEval finds converging evidence from multiple complementary assays as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED, accepting the characterization without challenge, with only minor presentation suggestions about statistical comparisons.

Both evaluate CMV-specific T-cell proliferation findings (C82, C92). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting the data directly demonstrates differential Ki67 expression. Peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED, accepting this as evidence for the IL-15-driven bystander activation hypothesis without challenge.

Both address the absence of SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell activation (C93-C95). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED based on ICS and RT-PCR data ruling out viral persistence. Peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED, accepting this negative finding as consistent with the bystander activation hypothesis.

Both evaluate innate immune cell populations (C58-C60). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting the negative findings establish specificity of T-cell activation. Peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED (C61 included in peer review), accepting the data but requesting additional analyses of regulatory T-cell phenotypes.

Both address immune fingerprints and T-cell activation patterns in severe disease (C3, C4, C44-C55). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED based on comprehensive flow cytometry and convergent evidence. Peer reviewers mark as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging 'convincing evidence' statistically but requesting context about mechanistic and biological significance since these assays aren't clinically routine. Peer review also includes cytokine findings (C62-C64) not in OpenEval R1.

Both evaluate cohort characteristics and study design (C35-C42). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting clear documentation and appropriate details. Peer reviewers also mark as SUPPORTED but note limitations including lack of racial diversity and unvaccinated status, requesting acknowledgment of these constraints. Peer review includes additional claims (C43, C46, C50) about cohort details.

Both address interpretive conclusions and study implications (C104-C106). OpenEval marks as SUPPORTED, noting reasonable inferences and appropriate caution. Peer reviewers mark as SUPPORTED, describing the work as 'important' with 'convincing evidence' of broad interest. Peer review includes C103 while OpenEval R14 includes additional interpretive claims (C98, C102).

OpenEval R10 addresses IFN-γ absence in severe patients (C63-C64) as a specific cytokine finding, marking as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes these claims as part of broader immune fingerprint evaluation marked as UNCERTAIN due to questions about mechanistic significance.

OpenEval evaluates sustained IP-10 elevation over time (C67) as SUPPORTED based on longitudinal Luminex data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific cytokine temporal pattern.

OpenEval evaluates background literature and established knowledge claims (C1-C2, C10-C25) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and standard literature review. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates literature-based discussion claims (C89-C91, C96-C97, C99-C100, C103) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate scholarly discussion. Peer review R10 includes C103 in broader conclusions evaluation, but no direct correspondence for other discussion claims.
